speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To better understand your bleeding issues, could you tell me if you have a family history of bleeding disorders or easy bruising? Also, have you noticed if the bleeding stops on its own or if it requires medical intervention to control?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you or your uncle have a history of bleeding into your joints, such as knees or elbows? Also, does the bleeding stop once you start clotting, or does it tend to restart later?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Persistent bleeding from gums following tooth extraction. I also have History of easy bruising, Family history of similar bleeding problems and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the bleeding from your gums eventually stop on its own, or does it require prolonged pressure or medical intervention to control? I would also like to know if you have experienced any spontaneous joint swelling or bleeding in the past. REQUEST TEST: Coagulation_panel

text: The prolonged PTT with normal PT and bleeding time strongly suggests a factor VIII or IX deficiency. Given the family history and joint symptoms, I will check specific factor levels. REQUEST TEST: Factor_VIII_level; Factor_IX_level

speaker: Doctor
text: Since Factor VIII and IX are normal, the isolated prolonged PTT suggests a deficiency in another intrinsic pathway factor, such as Factor XI, or the presence of an inhibitor. REQUEST TEST: Factor_XI_level

speaker: Doctor
text: The significantly low Factor XI level confirms the diagnosis of Factor XI deficiency, also known as Hemophilia C. DIAGNOSIS READY: Factor XI deficiency
